prelimsCapsule.coreConceptSummary: Article 371J was inserted into the Constitution of India by the Constitution (Ninety-Eighth Amendment) Act, 2012, to provide special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region (officially renamed Kalyan-Karnataka). It empowers the Governor to establish a separate development board and provides for local reservations in education and public employment.
highYieldFacts: Fact 1: Inserted via the 98th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2012, effective from January 2013.
Fact 2: Covers six backward districts of northern Karnataka: Gulbarga (Kalaburagi), Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal, Bellary (Ballari), and Bidar.
Fact 3: Empowers the President to direct the Governor of Karnataka to establish a separate development board for the region.
Fact 4: Provides for reservation of seats in educational institutions and state government jobs for persons belonging to the Kalyan-Karnataka region.
Fact 5: Recommendations for Article 371J originated from the D.M. Nanjundappa Committee report on regional imbalances.
trapsAndElimination: Trap 1: Confusing Article 371J (Karnataka) with Article 371D (Andhra Pradesh/Telangana) regarding educational and employment quotas. Article 371J specifically pertains to the backward districts of Northern Karnataka.

Trap 2: Assuming the development board is mandatory; the text states the President 'may' provide for the establishment of such a board, but once established, a report must be laid annually before the State Legislature.
keyArticlesOrStatutes: Article 371J of the Constitution of India

mainsFramework.inDepthTheoryHtml:
Origins and Evolution of Article 371J

The incorporation of Article 371J into the Indian Constitution was the culmination of decades of agitation by civil society, political leaders, and intellectuals from the erstwhile Hyderabad-Karnataka region. Historically, this region was a part of the princely state of Hyderabad under the Nizam, which was integrated into the Indian Union in 1948 via Operation Polo. Despite integration, the region lagged severely behind southern and coastal Karnataka in socio-economic development, per capita income, literacy, healthcare infrastructure, and public employment.

Institutional Architecture and Key Provisions

Article 371J endows specific mechanisms to rectify regional disparities:

  • Development Board: Provision for establishing a separate Kalyan-Karnataka Development Board (KKDB) to allocate funds specifically for developmental expenditure, ensuring equitable distribution.
  • Reservations in Education and Employment: Special reservation of seats in educational institutions and state civil services for students and residents belonging to the Kalyan-Karnataka region.
  • State Legislative Committee: Constitution of a separate committee of members of the State Legislative Assembly belonging to the region to monitor developmental activities.

Contemporary Challenges and Governance Bottlenecks

Despite statutory backing, implementation hurdles persist. Fund under-utilization, bureaucratic apathy from the state capital (Bengaluru), and inadequate technical capacity at the local district levels limit the transformative potential of KKDB. Furthermore, elite capture within the reserved quotas has sometimes alienated the most marginalized sections within the region itself.

dimensions.constitutional_or_legal: Exercise of constituent power via Article 371J balancing cooperative federalism and affirmative action for sub-regions.
dimensions.socio_economic: Bridging the Human Development Index (HDI) gap between northern and southern Karnataka districts, targeting education and healthcare deficits.
dimensions.administrative_governance: Empowerment of local administrative machinery, decentralized planning through the Kalyan-Karnataka Development Board, and legislative oversight.
dimensions.international_or_comparative: Aligns with global paradigms of addressing territorial inequality and spatial injustice, akin to devolution policies in unitary and federal states globally.

landmarkJudgmentsOrReports: High-Power Committee for Redressal of Regional Imbalances (D.M. Nanjundappa Committee Report, 2002)

prelims.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India has special provisions with respect to the State of Karnataka?
prelims.explanation: Article 371J was inserted by the 98th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2012, providing special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region. Article 371G relates to Mizoram, 371H to Arunachal Pradesh, and 371I to Goa.

mains.question: Asymmetrical federalism is the core of India's federal constitutional framework. Discuss the rationale and utility of special provisions for various states under Article 371.

modelMainsQA.question: Examine the socio-economic and political rationale behind the enactment of Article 371J for the Kalyan-Karnataka region. To what extent has it succeeded in bridging regional disparities? (150 Words, 10 Marks)

approach.intro: Define Article 371J and the context of the Kalyan-Karnataka region (98th Amendment, 2012).
approach.body: Discuss the rationale (historical backwardness, Nanjundappa Committee findings) and evaluate successes (jobs, education quotas, KKDB funding) versus challenges (bureaucratic bottlenecks, implementation gaps).
approach.conclusion: Emphasize holistic administrative capacity building and effective fund utilization to realize the vision of balanced regional development.

modelMainsQA.modelAnswerHtml:
Introduction: Article 371J, inserted via the 98th Constitutional Amendment Act (2012), embodies India's asymmetrical federalism by extending special provisions to six backward districts of northern Karnataka (Kalyan-Karnataka region) to eliminate regional imbalances.

Socio-Economic & Political Rationale:

  • Historical Legacy: Long-term neglect originating from erstwhile princely rule under the Nizam resulted in abysmal educational, health, and economic indicators.
  • Nanjundappa Committee Findings: The High-Power Committee (2002) scientifically proved deep inter-district disparities, necessitating constitutional intervention.

Assessment of Success:

  • Affirmative Action: Substantial reservation in educational institutions and state government jobs has created a burgeoning middle class in the region.
  • Dedicated Funding: The Kalyan-Karnataka Development Board (KKDB) has channeled targeted outlays towards rural infrastructure, irrigation, and skill development.

Persistent Challenges: Fund under-utilization, delayed bureaucratic sanctioning, and lack of localized planning capacities continue to dilute ground-level outcomes.

Conclusion: While Article 371J is a vital instrument for social justice, its true efficacy depends on rigorous legislative oversight, institutional capacity building, and decentralized governance to ensure equitable growth across Karnataka.

practiceMCQs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 371J of the Indian Constitution:
1. It was inserted by the Constitution (Ninety-Eighth Amendment) Act, 2012.
2. It applies to all districts of Karnataka with a special focus on the coastal region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceMCQs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct. Article 371J was inserted by the 98th Amendment Act, 2012. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 371J applies specifically to the six backward districts of the Hyderabad-Karnataka (Kalyan-Karnataka) region, not all districts or the coastal region.

practiceMCQs.question: Which of the following committees recommended measures for the redressal of regional imbalances in Karnataka, laying the groundwork for Article 371J?
practiceMCQs.explanation: The High-Power Committee for Redressal of Regional Imbalances headed by D.M. Nanjundappa (submitted in 2002) identified the backwardness of taluks in Karnataka and recommended special constitutional and financial safeguards.
